voiceGuidance: Warm, confident, grounded — a sharp analyst friend showing you something they genuinely find useful, not a hype reel. Measured pace ~150 words per minute, a slight slow-down on the key claims (cited answers, free, not investment advice). Let short sentences land; a beat between sections. Rising energy through the problem, calm clarity through the features and demo, a touch more warmth in the close. Never breathless, never salesy. Numbers spoken plainly so a first-time listener catches them.

segments.slideTitle: Public filings hold the truth. Reading them is the problem.
slideBullets: A single 10-K can run past three hundred pages of dense legal and financial text.
Professionals pay thousands a year for tools like AlphaSense and Fintool.
Everyone else gets raw EDGAR — the documents, with none of the answers.
segments.narration: Every public company tells you the truth about its business — in its SEC filings. The catch is reading them. A single annual report can run past three hundred pages of dense legal and financial language. Professionals pay thousands a year for research tools to cut through it. Everyone else is left with raw EDGAR — the filings themselves, and none of the answers.

segments.slideTitle: Ask a filing anything — and see the receipts.
slideBullets: Plain-English questions, answered from the filing's own text.
Every answer is grounded and cited — no hand-wavy hallucinations.
Powered by Claude, Anthropic's frontier AI model.
segments.narration: Start with the core feature: you can ask any filing a question. What are the biggest new risks this year? How did margins move? What did management actually say about guidance? StockHuntr answers in plain English, grounded in the filing's own words — with the receipts, so you can verify every claim. It's powered by Claude, Anthropic's frontier model.

segments.slideTitle: AI risk and concern scoring on every filing.
slideBullets: Claude compares risk factors across filings — new, removed, escalating.
Management sentiment, read from the MD&A on a clear scale.
One concern score tells you where to look first.
segments.narration: Beyond questions, StockHuntr scores every filing. It compares the risk factors against the company's previous report — surfacing risks that are new, that quietly disappeared, or that are escalating in tone. It reads management sentiment from the discussion section. And it rolls all of that up into a single concern score, so you instantly know which filings deserve a closer look.

segments.slideTitle: A research signal: 30-day alpha, not hype.
slideBullets: A model estimates each filing's 30-day return versus the S&P 500.
Trained on thousands of historical filings, backtested walk-forward.
A starting point for research — never investment advice.
segments.narration: For the market-minded, each analyzed filing also carries a thirty-day signal — the model's estimate of how the stock might move relative to the S&P 500 over the next month. It's trained on thousands of historical filings and backtested carefully. And we're deliberately honest about it: it's a research starting point, not a promise, and never investment advice.

segments.slideTitle: Built on primary sources — and open to developers.
slideBullets: SEC EDGAR filings, Yahoo Finance market data, Claude analysis.
A mixture-of-experts model behind the 30-day signal.
An MCP server and an open dataset — plug StockHuntr into your agents.
segments.narration: Under the hood, StockHuntr is built on primary sources — filings straight from SEC EDGAR, market data from Yahoo Finance, and analysis from Claude. The thirty-day signal comes from a mixture-of-experts model trained per sector and company size. And because this is as useful to machines as to people, there's an MCP server and an open dataset — so you can plug StockHuntr's filing intelligence straight into your own AI agents.
